messages:
alex: Quick follow-up from the RFC: we had two near-miss incidents where regional capacity and cost-tiering choices interacted badly with hedged fallbacks. Can we do a short design check here on a resilience-first contract for the policy engine?

maya: Yep. TL;DR of the issue: runtime returned a cheap variant in region A but suddenly latency spiked to p99=1200ms. Policy picked it because cost delta > threshold and didn't hedge. Frontend timed out.

sam: That matches the signal we saw in traces. We had no explicit capacity_score exposed by that runtime variant so the policy assumed it was healthy.

eli: Proposal: require runtimes to publish two lightweight signals in the route descriptor: "capacity_score" (0-1) and "observed_p99_ms". Policy must treat missing capacity_score as conservative (0.3) not optimistic.

jordan: I like forcing a conservative default. Also add a staleness TTL on signals (e.g., 15s) — if a signal is older, it should be aged toward conservative. That prevents stale probes from masking a hot GPU.

rachel: What about cost-driven tie-breakers? We still want to prefer cheaper options when safe. Could the policy use a multi-stage check: 1) prefer same-region with capacity_score > 0.6 and p99_ms < 300; 2) otherwise hedge to N+1 region where cost delta < 20%?

alex: Yes. Sketch of decision rule I had in mind (pseudo-config):
```
selection: 
  - if region == preferred and capacity_score >= 0.6 and observed_p99_ms <= 300: choose(primary)
  - else if capacity_score >= 0.4 and cost_delta <= 0.15: try(primary)
  - else: hedge(N=1, fallback_policy: prefer lower latency even if cost + <= 0.25)
```

maya: Two caveats: (1) observed_p99_ms requires consistent measurement window (we use 1min rolling p99) and (2) we need safe defaults for telemetry missingness.

sam: Also need to think about atomicity and rollout surface: we can't change the contract for all runtimes at once. We should support backward-compatible semantics: runtimes that don't send capacity_score get mapped to the conservative default, and config flags allow tenants to opt into the new hedging behavior.

eli: Operationally, adding these signals will change admission. Ops note: we'll need a simulation run against last 30d of traffic to validate unit economic impact. I can run a sim if we produce a canonical mapping from runtime probe -> capacity_score.

jordan: Implementation boundaries: this should be in policy engine (compiler + runtime adapter). Two possible places: (A) policy compiler inserts a small adapter that normalizes runtime signals to the canonical fields before eval, or (B) each runtime is responsible for returning canonical fields. I prefer (A) for safety; adapter can include per-runtime heuristics and versioned mappers.

rachel: Adapter (A) lets us ship faster. But we must standardize metric names so console/telemetry works consistently. Suggest canonical names: runtime.capacity_score, runtime.p99_ms, runtime.signal_ts.

alex: Good. Decisions so far:
- Require normalized signals in policy evaluation path (via adapter)
- Default missing/old signals -> conservative capacity_score = 0.3, p99_ms = high (9999)
- Add hedging clause configurable per-tenant with default N=1 and cost_delta cap 0.25

maya: For testing: add a small harness that can replay a seq of routing events and assert SLA breaches under candidate policies. We should include a few attack patterns (fast cost-change, probe-staleness, partial-region outage).

sam: I'll add unit tests in the policy-compiler repo and a sim job in infra-sim. We should also add an integration test that runs on staging and compares latency/cost before/after rollout for a synthetic load.

eli: Telemetry: add these new metrics to /observability:
- routing.policy.decision.reason
- runtime.capacity_score (tagged by region, runtime-version)
- runtime.p99_ms
- routing.hedge_count

jordan: Ops-bot: please create an incident-style alert for sudden drop in average capacity_score per-region > 30% relative to baseline (1m window).

ops-bot: @jordan created alert: "region.capacity_score_drop" threshold=30% window=60s. Runbook: follow regional-capacity playbook, add temporary hedging override.

rachel: Minor UX ask for Console: allow per-route preview of the normalized signals and simulated decisions for a given time-window. That'll make it easier to justify hedging to customers.

alex: Action items (owners):
- eli: produce canonical mapping doc + sim inputs (ETA: Thu)
- sam: add unit tests + sim harness PR (ETA: Fri)
- maya: update policy compiler adapter plan + backwards compat note (ETA: Wed)
- rachel: mockups for console preview + telemetry dashboards (ETA: Mon)
- jordan: ops alert created (done)

maya: One last tradeoff to call out: adding hedging will increase cross-region traffic and egress costs. We must make sure the Optimize tooling can simulate cost tradeoffs per-tenant and provide an opt-out.

alex: Agreed. We'll make hedging opt-in per-tenant initially and enable a global default after we validate sim results. :thumbsup:

sam: SGTM. If nobody objects, I'll open the follow-up RFC PR with decision record and attach sim plan.

eli: :+1:

rachel: :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks all — good checkin.
